result.text: An e-commerce company has a comprehensive order fulfillment process: When a customer places an order, the system records the order details.
Payment processing begins.
If the payment fails, the customer is notified, and the process ends.
Upon successful payment, the inventory system checks stock availability.
If items are out of stock, a back-order is initiated, and the customer is informed about the delay.
The process continues once the back-order is received and all required items are available in stock.
In-stock items are picked from the warehouse.
Quality control checks are performed on the picked items.
Packaging is done, including gift wrapping if the customer requested it.
Meanwhile, the shipping department prepares shipping documents and labels.
If the order is international, customs documentation is prepared.
Once packaging and shipping documents are ready, the order is dispatched.
The system sends a shipping confirmation to the customer.
After dispatch, the system updates the inventory levels.
A follow-up email for feedback is sent directly after confirming the successful delivery.
If the customer reports any issues upon delivery, a returns process is initiated, which includes: Sending a return shipping label.
Receiving returned items.
Inspecting returned items.
Processing a refund or replacement.

args.text: When a process description says that an external participant reports an issue and this report initiates a process, model the report as an event rather than as a task.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already addresses modeling an external report that initiates a process.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

args.text: When an external participant's report or message triggers work within an already-running process, model the occurrence as a message catch event, not as a task or a new process start event.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers modeling reports that trigger process work.

result.rule: When the description states that an external request or inquiry starts the process: Model the trigger as a start event, followed by a distinct task for receiving or handling the request.

When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
When the description states an occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with a concise phrase naming that trigger rather than a generic label.

When the description states that a participant may perform an optional activity after the main process outcome has been reached: Model that activity as an optional continuation of the same process, rather than as a new process initiated by the activity.

args.text: When naming BPMN elements, use concise labels that preserve the description's meaning without adding unsupported details; start and end event labels should match the described event rather than use generic labels.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance covers naming fidelity or event labels before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Declare the BPMN model namespace http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL and a non-empty targetNamespace on bpmn:definitions.

result.rule: When the description states an occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with a concise phrase naming that trigger rather than a generic label.

When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.

When the description explicitly states the outcome that marks the process as complete: label the end event with a concise phrase that faithfully names that outcome, rather than a generic label or an unnecessarily detailed restatement

When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
